newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Lacklustre day ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Lacklustre day ahead of data.

text.p: Asia's debt markets had a lacklustre day as banks sat back and waited for U.S. economic data due later this week, bankers said on Thursday.
One banker who focuses on U.S. and Hong Kong dollar debt issues, said he had done no deals all week, and was waiting for the U.S. May wage and payrolls report on Friday.
Until the numbers arrive he expected secondary market debt to range trade and was not bringing any new issues.
Early responses to Hutchison Whampoa Ltd's HK$10 billion refinancing are good, a banker close to the deal said.
"Hutchison is one of those names banks would like to bank with," he said. Responses are due on Friday.
Bankers said they expected the recent wave of corporate refinancings, to tail off ahead of the handover, as potential borrowers monitored interest rates medium-term direction.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
"The market will probably consolidate...the flurry of activity for the last few weeks, for the last few months, exhausted quite a few people, including ourselves," one said.
"July is a month for parties," a treasurer with an Australian financial institution bank said.
But bankers predicted more interest in mortgage securitisations, following recent successful issues.
"I think a lot of banks have been waiting for the mortgage corporation too long," said one.
Hong Kong's Exchange Fund advisory committee last year approved the setting up of a mortgage corporation loosely modelled on FannieMae in the United States.
The banker said many banks were close to their 40 percent limit for mortgages and wanted to hive some off so they could benefit from the booming property market.
Both Sanwa's deal, and an earlier mortgage-backed floating- rate note (FRN) from Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd benefited from guarantees from MBIA Assurance.

Confidence in Hong Kong was encouraging monoline insurers like MBIA Assurance to enhance local credits despite the ceiling imposed by Hong Kong's A-plus long-term foreign currency rating (from Standard & Poor's) and A3 long-term bonds rating (Moody's Investors Service), he said.
In other Asian news, Kingboard Chemical Holdings has mandated ABN Amro to arrange a HK$150 million two-tranche loan facility, ABN Amro said.
Tranche A is a HK$100 million term loan, repayable in five equal semi-annual instalments after a grace period of 12 months from loan signing date. Both tranches are for three years.
Tranche B is HK$50 million revolving credit. Repayment is in bullet form. The interest margin is 135 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Fees are 50 basis points for lead managers committing HK$21 million to HK$25 million, and 40 basis points for managers committing HK$15 million to HK$20 million.
PT Tjahja Sakti Motor Corporation launched a US$25 million term loan facility.
The two-year loan pays a margin of 75 basis points over the Singapore Interbank Offered Rate (SIBOR) for direct lenders and 120 basis points over SIBOR for tax-absorbed lenders.
Shinhan Bank launched a 300 million Deutsche mark three-year Euro at an issue price of 101.188, and 99,5755 reoffer.
